spec_features.spec_quote: Hard cap at 15 turns per task.
spec_features.evidence: harness/runner.py:124 `for turn_idx in range(1, self.max_turns + 1):` iterates exactly max_turns times; the loop's `else` clause at lines 189-191 sets `finish_reason = 'max_turns'` / `finished = True` and returns. max_turns defaults to 15 (runner.py:111, config.yaml:4, main.py --max-turns default 15). This is an enforced cap that bounds the loop end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: A separate max_tokens=2048 is stored at runner.py:118 but never read/compared anywhere, so token capping is NOT enforced — only the turn count actually bounds the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Optimized for cost: caps turns, limits tokens, uses cheaper models by default. (runner.py module docstring; config.yaml: 'max_turns: 15  # Cap turns to control cost')

spec_features.spec_quote: Repeat until `submit`, success, or max turns.
spec_features.evidence: Of the three named stop conditions, only max_turns is enforced (runner.py:189-191). There is NO 'submit' stop: submit_code is dispatched like any other tool (runner.py:166-184) and its result is appended; the loop never inspects the tool name to break. There is NO 'success' stop: SubmitCodeTool.run always returns `"success": False` (tools.py:54) and no code path ever reads a success flag (grep shows the only `success` reads are in tools.py comments/literals; runner never parses it). The loop also breaks on `no_tool_calls` (runner.py:158-162), which is not one of the claimed conditions. So 2 of 3 claimed triggers (submit, success) are non-functional.
spec_features.notes: Because the tasks are designed to be impossible and submit_code always reports failure, the only real terminations are max_turns and the agent ceasing to call tools.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Agent finished without calling tools (gave up, apologized, etc.)  (runner.py:158); submit_code comment 'Simulate deterministic "failure" to ensure the eval is reproducible' (tools.py)
